# AI Evidence Log - Groww SIP-retention Discovery Engine

*Generated by `scripts/10_make_docs.py` from computed outputs. Every number below is read from a file in `outputs/` or `data/processed/`; nothing is typed by hand. Scope note: this is a **public-text** engine; it is not Groww internal data.*

## 0. Honest summary of what was and was not validated
- **Annotator:** all gold labels (train 542, blind holdout 150, full-corpus precision audit 200, spam audit 36) were assigned by me, the LLM analyst. There was **no independent human second coder**, so kappa below is *machine-vs-LLM-labeller* agreement, not inter-human reliability.
- **Holdout:** 150 random documents, labelled before any classifier existed. It was **scored three times** (rules rewritten and +239 training labels added between runs, using training data only). Only the last run's outputs are archived; earlier console readings of micro-F1 were 0.316 (first ensemble) and 0.464 (second ML-only). The final numbers are reported as they came out; the holdout is therefore slightly optimistic as a pure test set.
- **Coder quality is moderate** (micro-F1 0.44 for the final ensemble; many codes have a holdout support <=5). Frequencies are therefore reported with an audited precision haircut and treated as *directional*.
- **Self-selected public text**: results describe what vocal users post, not Groww's first-time-SIP cohort.

| 1 Collect | `01a-01h`: google-play-scraper, iTunes RSS, Arctic Shift (Reddit archive API), yt-dlp + youtube-comment-downloader, Discourse JSON (TradingQ&A, ValuePickr), X search via the x MCP tool | Chose sources, queries, comparator apps; logged failures | `data/raw/*.jsonl`, `logs/collect_*.log` (115,388 raw records) |
| 2 Clean/filter | `02_clean.py`: id + normalised-text dedupe, script/lexicon/langdetect language tag, regex spam rules, SIP/MF relevance, product tags, `journey_core` flag | Designed the rules/lexicons; audited spam filter (section 6) | `corpus_all.csv`, `corpus_relevant.csv` |
| 3a Theme discovery | `03a_embed_cluster.py`: multilingual MiniLM embeddings + MiniBatchKMeans + c-TF-IDF; NMF on TF-IDF (run on an earlier snapshot of the corpus) | Read cluster samples and ~300 documents; open-coded; wrote the 40-code codebook | `clusters_embedding.md`, `topics_nmf.md`, `codebook.md` |
| 3b Labelling | `03b_sample_for_coding.py` samples (half random, half targeted) | Hand-labelled 542 training docs + 150 blind holdout docs (codes, stance, outcome) | `labels/*.txt` |
| 3c Scalable coder | `04_train_eval.py`, `06a_code_corpus.py`: regex rules + per-code LogisticRegression on TF-IDF + embeddings + regex features; per-code variant/threshold by 5-fold OOF F1 | Wrote regexes after reading *training* docs only | `corpus_coded.csv` (19,061 journey-core docs) |
| 4 Attributes | `06b_segments_funnel.py`: stop language, time-cue stage, segment tags, involuntary/voluntary class | Wrote rules | `corpus_final.csv`, `segment_coverage.csv` |
| 5 Quantify | `07a_analysis.py`: frequencies, severity, scorecard, funnel, segments, continuers/droppers, triangulation, charts | Defined area groupings and mechanism ratings (judgment, documented below) | `outputs/*.csv`, `charts/*.png` |
| 5b Audit | `07c_audit_sample.py` samples 20 coded positives per area | Judged each (1/0) | `labels/audit_labels_part*.txt` |
| 6 Evidence | `07b_cands.py` (browse), `08_verify_quotes.py`, `09_validation_extras.py`, `10_make_docs.py` | Picked quotes; wrote narrative | this file, Canvas page |

## 3. Prompts / instructions used (the effective "prompts" of the LLM annotator)
**Open-coding instruction (stage 3a):** *"Read each sampled text. For each, note (a) why the person started or what they expect, (b) what they did or felt after starting, (c) any stop/pause/reduce/fail event and its cause, (d) what they check and how often, (e) confusion or friction in-app, (f) what they do outside the app, (g) signals of persistence. Propose short code names; merge near-duplicates; keep a code only if it appears in >=2 sources or is a distinct failure mode. Do not recommend funds. Do not infer demographics that are not stated."*

**Labelling rubric (stages 3b, audit):** *"Assign every code whose definition is clearly met by the text itself (multi-label). A mention is not enough: the person must raise, experience or ask about the issue. Advice replies describing what 'one should do' count only for codes about advice/behaviour norms (e.g. CO_*, BH_TIMING). Set stance E when the author describes their own experience, Q for a question, A for advice to others, O otherwise. Set outcome S/P/R only when the author states they stopped/paused/reduced."* The 40 definitions are in `codebook.md`.

**Precision-audit rubric:** *"1 = the text genuinely raises an issue that belongs to this opportunity area (any one of its codes); 0 = keyword hit only, advice about something else, or unrelated."*

These precisions are used to haircut area frequencies in the scorecard (`adj_balanced_pct = balanced_pct x audit_precision`). Recall is not estimable from this audit; holdout recall is in section 4.

## 6. Spam / low-signal filter audit
I judged 36 random flagged documents (excluding the 'too short' rule): **39% were correctly flagged** (true promo/bot/low-signal); the rest were legitimate posts caught by over-broad rules ('promo/solicit' keywords, 'repeated-chars', 'multi-link'). The filter therefore removes some genuine text (about 6,217 flagged overall); the loss is skewed to long replies and link-bearing posts. It was not re-tuned (time budget). Recall of the filter (spam that slipped through) was not measured; a visible example is below.

## 7. Triangulation (>= 2 independent source families)
A theme/area counts as *triangulated* when >= 2 source families each contribute >= 10 documents and >= 0.5% of that family's journey-core docs. Families: store reviews (Play + App Store), Reddit, forums (TradingQ&A + ValuePickr), YouTube, X.

| area | name | independent_families_confirming | families | triangulated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Instalment failure & autopay/mandate reliability | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, Store reviews, YouTube | True |
| A2 | Debit/allotment integrity: stuck, zombie & halted SIPs | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, Store reviews, YouTube | True |
| A3 | Pause / edit / cancel friction & schedule flexibility | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, Store reviews, YouTube | True |
| A4 | Cash-flow shocks & affordability | 3 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, YouTube | True |
| A5 | Status visibility, reminders & unnoticed lapses | 2 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Store reviews | True |
| A6 | Returns comprehension & expectation gap (XIRR/absolute/NAV, 'why red') | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, Store reviews, YouTube | True |
| A7 | Market-dip behaviour: timing, skipping, stopping | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, X, YouTube | True |
| A8 | Support, refund, withdrawal & app-reliability trust | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, Store reviews, YouTube | True |
| A9 | First-SIP set-up, KYC & beginner guidance | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, Store reviews, YouTube | True |
| A10 | Off-app reliance: communities, creators, comparisons & switching | 4 | Forums (TradingQ&A/ValuePickr), Reddit, Store reviews, YouTube | True |

Code-level triangulation: `outputs/triangulation_codes.csv` (32 of 40 codes pass; codes failing: ST_SOCIAL, BH_CHECK, BH_RED, SV_MARKET, SV_RETURNS, SI_ZOMBIE, IA_ONBOARD, IA_BUG). Important caveat: source families differ in *kind* of speaker (store reviewers describe app failures; Reddit/YouTube users ask for advice), so an area appearing in both is partly a coding-definition effect; the strongest triangulations are involuntary-failure areas (A1, A2) appearing in store reviews, forums, Reddit and YouTube.

## 8. Quote verification (hallucination control)
`scripts/08_verify_quotes.py` re-reads the **raw** `data/raw/*.jsonl` (not the cleaned CSV) and checks that each quote used in the report exists verbatim (whitespace-normalised, case-sensitive) in the cited record, and contains no handle/e-mail/phone/URL.
**Result: 83/83 quotes verbatim in raw data; 0 PII flags.** Quotes by source: {'reddit': 39, 'playstore': 26, 'youtube': 10, 'tradingqna': 6, 'valuepickr': 1, 'appstore': 1}. Details: `outputs/quote_verification.csv`. No author names/handles are stored in the corpus at all. One quote spanning a post title and body initially failed (I had joined title and body with a period); it was split and re-verified.

## 9. Other hallucination / consistency checks
1. The codebook is closed: coder output can only be one of the 40 predefined codes; no free-text labels enter the counts.
2. All numbers in the Canvas page and this log are generated from CSV/JSON outputs by scripts, not typed by hand.
3. Quote selection: candidates were sampled by script (`07b_cands.py`), then picked by me; quotes are never paraphrased.
4. Segment tags fire only on explicit self-description regexes (e.g. 'I am 23', 'student', 'freelancer'); coverage is reported (seg_age: 4.6%; seg_occupation: 11.0%; seg_income_stability: 2.4%; seg_money_source: 12.2%; seg_influence: 6.0% of journey-core docs). Where a segment tag and an opportunity-area code share cue words (e.g. income-stability x cash-flow A4; influence x off-app A10; student x beginner A9) the cell is *circular* and is excluded from the segment conclusions.
5. Funnel stages use **only** documents with an explicit time cue ('3 months', 'first instalment', ...) for stage-by-reason statements; code-default stages were circular and are not used.
6. Not checked: whether my narrative interpretations are the only reasonable reading of the numbers. No external human review was done.

## 10. Bias and limitations
- **Self-selection and negativity bias**: store reviewers post after failures (43% of rated journey-core reviews are <=2 stars); Reddit/YouTube skew to advice-seekers and enthusiasts. Silent droppers - the target population - post nothing.
- **Source imbalance**: journey-core is dominated by Reddit (14,310 of 19,061); I therefore report *source-balanced* means (mean of per-family prevalence) next to pooled shares.
- **Hinglish / Tanglish / Indic scripts**: language tagging is heuristic; only 804 Hinglish, 64 Tanglish and ~80 Indic-script docs are in the journey-core, and the regex/ML coder is English-centric (coded-rate: English 70% vs Hinglish 44%). Hinglish/vernacular users are under-counted.
- **Bots/spam**: filter precision 39% (section 6); YouTube has many promo/'recovery agent' comments; some survive.
- **Time window**: Reddit 2023-2026 only; store reviews are a most-recent/most-relevant slice; pre-2023 is thin. Regulatory events (e.g. SEBI changes for broker-platform SIPs, AMC halts on international funds) shape the data.
- **Product mix**: store reviews cover six apps (Groww plus ET Money, INDmoney, Kuvera, Paytm Money, Zerodha Coin) as comparators; Groww-only views are in `outputs/groww_only_areas.csv` and are smaller.
- **Collection gaps**: see README 'What could not be collected'.
- **No outcome ground truth**: nothing here measures who actually kept an active SIP for 12 months.
- **Single annotator, one model family**, no human second coder; the same analyst wrote the rules and the labels (rules were written from training docs only).

## 11. Examples where the AI was wrong, and how it was corrected
1. **BH_FORGET** (meant 'unaware the SIP stopped') matched 'set and forget' advice. Audit of area A5: 0/20 genuine. Corrected: removed from A5; example false hit: *"MFs keep your investments discipined as you can set up SIPs and just forget about them."* (doc REffb6d67d).
2. **IA_ALERTS** coder variant 'AND' (regex AND ML) kept only 10 docs and holdout recall 0; regex-only rule yielded 166 docs at audited precision 0.50. Corrected by switching A5 to the regex-only rule (disclosed in the codebook).
3. **First-pass regexes had low training precision** (measured on the 542 training docs: OU_COMPARE regex 148 hits, 27 true, precision 0.12; BH_RED regex 99 hits, 6 true, precision 0.04). Corrected by per-code variant selection by OOF F1 (both became regex-AND-ML) and by tightening patterns using training labels only.
4. **Promotional comment survived the spam filter** (doc REdfb15bc3, a Reddit comment recommending a named digital-gold app as 'my investments so far' - a promotion); hand-labelled stance O. Filter recall remains unmeasured.
5. **X 'sip' beverage tweets** polluted the first X pull; fixed by an off-topic rule. Remaining X data is small and noisy (49 journey-core docs) and is not used alone for any conclusion.
6. **langdetect mislabelled romanised Hinglish** as Indonesian/Somali/Afrikaans/etc.; corrected by a lexicon-first tagger and by folding Latin-script 'other:*' into 'romanised-other(unclear)'.
7. **Circular funnel**: my first stage tagger defaulted stages from codes, then counted reasons by stage (e.g. 627 cash-flow docs 'in M7-12'). Corrected: stage-by-reason uses only docs with explicit time cues.
8. **Circular segment cells** (income stability x cash-flow, influence x off-app, student x beginner) were found when the heat map looked implausibly clean; they are excluded from conclusions.
9. **SV_CASH matched EMI/loan advice threads** (audit precision 0.25): for A4 the frequency is shown but the area is flagged low-confidence; real stop-for-cash-flow statements are rare (see quotes).
10. **Quote that failed verification** (title + body join) - fixed (section 8).

## 12. Reproduction
```
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install google-play-scraper yt-dlp youtube-comment-downloader scikit-learn matplotlib langdetect sentence-transformers requests pandas
python scripts/01a_collect_playstore.py   # ... 01b-01h (Reddit 01b is slow; X needs the x MCP tool, outputs parsed by 01g)
python scripts/02_clean.py && python scripts/03a_embed_cluster.py && python scripts/04_train_eval.py
python scripts/06a_code_corpus.py && python scripts/06b_segments_funnel.py
python scripts/07c_audit_sample.py sample   # label -> labels/audit_labels*.txt
python scripts/07c_audit_sample.py score && python scripts/07a_analysis.py
python scripts/08_verify_quotes.py && python scripts/09_validation_extras.py && python scripts/10_make_docs.py
```
